name: AlGhamdi Company for Sanitary Wares       شركة الغامدي وشركاه للأدوات الصحية
reason: Saudi-HQ'd (Riyadh, est. 1970) sole Kingdom agent for American Standard/Ideal Standard and Bobrick sanitary ware. Product line is toilets, wash basins, mixers, kitchen sinks, taps and bathroom fixtures/fittings for construction and renovation projects, an explicitly named hard-fail category ('sanitary ware' is listed by name in the Gate 2 exclusions) regardless of the 'virtual showroom'/'SHOP' branding on the site.

name: Ansar Group of Companies
reason: Doha, Qatar-HQ'd holding company (est. 1980s, formalized 1987) whose corporate site explicitly organizes the group into three co-equal pillars: Retail (Superstores/Ansar Gallery), Hospitality (Hotels), and Real Estate. As the holding entity (distinct from the separately-evaluated Ansar Gallery retail row in this same batch), it fails on category: hospitality and real estate are both explicit hard-fail categories and are presented as core, not incidental, business lines.

name: Araboil
reason: WebSearch confirms this is Arab Oil Fuel Company, established 2022 to provide vehicle fuel services in Saudi Arabia. Fuel/gas-station services are not an approved retail category (not fashion, beauty, grocery/F&B, or electronics/furniture); it is automotive-fuel adjacent, a hard-fail vertical. The domain is also now a dead/parked ad-redirect page, so gate 4 would independently fail too.

name: مكتبه جرير
reason: The domain does not correspond to the stated company (Jarir Bookstore) at all. arabplaces.com is a pan-Arab business-listings/directory website with country subdomains, not a retailer selling any product, let alone one in an approved category.

name: Areej AL Khaleej  |  اريج الخليج
reason: Domain returns a persistent server-level 403 Forbidden (Hostinger/LiteSpeed hosting) on https, http, and http/1.1. A WebSearch cross-check per protocol did not find a confirmed live storefront for this exact domain; results were ambiguous/conflicting, surfacing an apparently unrelated same-named 'Areej Al Khaleej' auto sales/rental and construction group plus unrelated Areej-branded fashion influencers, with no verifiable link to this domain. No live site content could be confirmed anywhere.

name: Armah Sports Company
reason: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia-HQ'd business that curates international fitness brands and designs, builds, and manages gym/fitness facilities for club operators across the GCC -- a B2B franchise/fit-out/management services business, not a consumer retailer of sporting goods or apparel. No product catalog or cart exists; only a corporate contact page.

name: Arriyadh Roaster محمصة الرياض
reason: Riyadh-founded (2019) specialty coffee roaster/retailer running on Salla (confirmed Saudi e-commerce SaaS platform with real cart), with an extensive multi-category catalog (espresso, Turkish coffee, capsules, single-origin beans by country, matcha, chocolate, grinders, filters, bags, cups) well past the 50-SKU floor, plus a wholesale arm (1,100+ wholesale clients) and 900 tons/year roasting capacity. Coffee is a high-frequency consumable, correctly fitting the grocery/F&B repeat-purchase bucket (prior category tag of 'sporting_toys_books' was mistaken). || CROSS-VERIFICATION (independent 2nd pass): Gate 2: the original reason itself states a wholesale arm serving 1,100+ wholesale clients plus 900 tons/year roasting, and the brand is resold through third-party retail platforms (wtr.sa, icup.sa); a hybrid B2C/B2B model that supplies other businesses is hard-excluded even with a genuine DTC arm.

name: شركة عثمان الزامل واخوانه
reason: Dammam, Saudi Arabia-HQ'd (est. 1981) trading company supplying building materials, safety equipment, and industrial materials, with its own online store explicitly branded 'Al-Zamil Store for Building Materials and Safety' -- a textbook construction-materials/industrial-supply hard-fail, confirmed even at the retail-store level.

name: Ashley Homestore | KSA
reason: ashley.sa itself is only a bare store-locator page, but WebSearch confirms the Saudi Ashley Furniture HomeStore franchise is operated by Hamad M. Alrugaib & Sons Trading Co. (Al Rugaib Furniture), a Saudi company established 1958 in Al Khobar -- a genuinely Saudi-HQ'd franchisee holding local rights to the foreign Ashley brand (passes gate 1, the same pattern as a Saudi conglomerate holding local IKEA/Circle K rights). The same operator's real transactional storefront at store.ashley.sa is a live Shopify site with a full cart/checkout flow (SAR pricing, free-shipping threshold) and a large multi-category furniture catalog (living room, bedroom, dining, lighting, home office, outdoor, rugs), comfortably over the 50-SKU floor. || CROSS-VERIFICATION (independent 2nd pass): Gate 6: a US global-brand (Ashley) storefront operated by Saudi franchisee Al Rugaib (Hamad M. Alrugaib & Sons, Al Khobar 1958). The underlying operation qualifies and Gate 1 is fine, but as a foreign-brand storefront it should consolidate under its Saudi operator Al Rugaib (a distinct furniture company that also runs its own-brand stores) rather than stand alone as 'Ashley KSA'; standalone-versus-consolidate status is unresolved.

name: Asklan Trading & Agriculture W.L.L
reason: Doha, Qatar-HQ'd (est. 1991) landscaping and irrigation contractor prequalified with ASHGAL, the Ministry of Municipality, QatarEnergy and other government bodies, executing projects 'as a main contractor and as sub-contractor.' Its 'Trading' arm supplies landscape/irrigation materials and plants to its own contracting projects, not direct consumer retail -- a B2B contracting/services business.

name: Aster Pharmacy - صيدلية استر
reason: The KSA pharmacy rollout is a joint venture between Aster DM Healthcare and Abdulmohsin Al Hokair Holding Group, but the operating brand, healthcare-group systems, and 38-year history are Aster DM Healthcare's, whose global origin and HQ (1987) is the UAE (Dubai). Independent press coverage frames it as 'UAE's Aster DM to open 250 plus pharmacies in Saudi Arabia,' i.e. a UAE-HQ'd group entering Saudi via a local joint-venture partner -- the explicit fail pattern (a store merely run by a UAE-HQ'd group fails, even with a local partner), distinct from a Saudi conglomerate independently holding franchise rights to a foreign brand.

name: ATHR Gallery
reason: A Saudi (Jeddah-oriented) contemporary art gallery representing artists for exhibitions and international art fairs (Art Basel), plus an art-storage-depot service. Fine-art gallery representation is not one of the approved retail categories; the presence of a generic Cart/Checkout widget does not change the underlying business, which is curated art representation, not general retail.

name: ايسوزو العيسى | Alissa Isuzu
reason: Confirmed via WebSearch as Alissa Universal Motors (AUM), the authorized Isuzu dealer in Saudi Arabia since 1985 (member of the Abdullatif Alissa Group), selling Isuzu pick-ups and light/medium/heavy-duty trucks. Automotive dealer -- explicit hard-fail category.

name: Auto Mall
reason: Confirmed via WebSearch as a spare auto-parts dealer/distributor operating since 1964, with showrooms in Dammam and Riyadh plus 12 warehouses across Saudi Arabia. Automotive parts dealer/distributor -- explicit hard-fail category.

name: Autozone Balubaid
reason: New-car dealership (اوتوزون) under the Balubaid Group, with 70+ years in the automotive sector and 30+ branches across 13 Saudi cities, selling Toyota, Hyundai, Honda, Kia, Isuzu, and other brands, plus vehicle financing. Automotive dealer -- explicit hard-fail category.

name: Auto Z Automotive Group W.L.L.
reason: Live WordPress site confirms this is a used-car dealership/showroom in Doha, Qatar. Automotive dealers are an explicit Gate 2 hard fail regardless of how real or live the operation is.

name: Baazeem Trading Company
reason: Live site is a pure corporate/B2B brand-portfolio site for an FMCG distributor, listing 13 distributed food/consumer brands with an explicit "distribution channels" nav item and no shop, cart, or checkout anywhere on the domain. Wholesale/trading/distribution (B2B) is an explicit Gate 2 hard fail.

name: Al Babtain Group
reason: Al Babtain Group is a large Kuwait-HQ'd conglomerate whose core historic business and largest division is automotive distribution (Infiniti, Nissan, Renault dealerships), alongside IT, investment, real estate, finance, and industrial divisions. Automotive dealer/distributor is an explicit Gate 2 hard fail regardless of the group's other, larger scale.

name: باك كمفورت - Backcomfort
reason: Confirmed live, functioning e-commerce site (Magento-style, real add-to-cart), but the entire catalog is confined to one narrow wellness-seating/sleep niche: massage chairs, office chairs, recliner chairs, and sleep products only, with no broader home-goods range. Like the confirmed-fail patterns for lighting-only, flooring-only, and tires/batteries-only stores, these are big-ticket items bought once every several years, unable to sustain the repeat customer engagement a CDP platform needs.

name: Al Baladi Holding
reason: This domain is the parent holding company's corporate/portfolio website (Home, About Us, Company Profile, Companies pages only), distinct from its retail operating brand BaladiMart/Baladi Express (separately captured and verified IN as baladiexpress.com in this same batch). The holding entity's own site has no cart or checkout; its 30+ company portfolio spans hotels/hospitality and limousine transport (non-qualifying) alongside hypermarkets, supermarkets, department stores, bakeries and restaurants (qualifying) -- but no live transactional storefront exists on baladiholding.com itself, so it fails on digital channel rather than an unambiguous category call.

name: Balsam Medical Care
reason: Balsam Medical is a Saudi hospital/medical-complex/clinic group covering general medicine, family medicine, pediatrics, OB/GYN, dentistry, ophthalmology, dermatology and orthopedics, with pharmacy only one part of a hospital-led portfolio rather than a standalone retail pharmacy chain. Healthcare/clinics/hospitals is an explicit Gate 2 hard fail (only retail pharmacy chains pass). The live domain itself is also a login-gated internal portal, not a public storefront.

name: Balsharaf Group
reason: Balsharaf is a genuine large FMCG manufacturer/distributor/retailer (chain of food stores in Riyadh since 1955, distribution to 16,000 retail outlets, manufacturing in KSA/Egypt/India), but balsharaf.com.sa itself is a static single-page corporate profile (About/Founder/Leaders/Businesses/Products/Retail/Media/Contact/Portal tabs) with product images filed under a "distribution" showcase and a B2B "/portal" link, not a consumer cart or checkout. No transactional online store was found anywhere on this domain.

name: Bastana International Company Ltd
reason: Bastana is fundamentally a landscaping/garden design-build-maintain contractor for government and private-sector projects in Saudi Arabia (45+ private projects, 6M+ sqm maintained, government classification since 2013) -- a B2B contracting/services business, an explicit Gate 2 hard fail. It does run a small ancillary online plant nursery claiming 250+ products, but this is a minor secondary offering under the same domain that does not redefine the primary identity of the landscaping contractor.

name: BATOOK HOLDING COMPANY
reason: Batook is a chewing-gum manufacturer and wholesale/retail trading group, not a direct-to-consumer retailer. The site is a corporate brand-portfolio page with zero cart, checkout, or pricing anywhere -- manufacturing and wholesale/trading distribution are both explicit Gate 2 hard-fail categories.
